name: Hereditary Macrothrombocytopenia with Mutations in MYH9

criteria.description: Presence of thrombocytopenia with abnormally large platelets on peripheral blood smear
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the MYH9 gene
Detection of characteristic Döhle-like inclusion bodies in neutrophils
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of thrombocytopenia with large platelets plus identification of a pathogenic MYH9 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing; inclusion bodies and family history support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Large platelets with low platelet count are hallmark features.
Characteristic cytoplasmic inclusions seen on blood smear.

common.notes: Includes easy bruising, epistaxis, and mucosal bleeding.
Progressive hearing impairment in some patients.
Proteinuria and progressive kidney disease may develop.
Symptoms related to low platelet count.

occasional.notes: Non-specific symptom related to chronic disease.

rare.notes: Advanced kidney disease in a minority of patients.

laboratory: Thrombocytopenia with giant platelets on peripheral blood smear
Presence of Döhle-like inclusion bodies in neutrophils
imaging: Renal ultrasound may show structural abnormalities in advanced disease
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in MYH9 gene (e.g., missense mutations affecting non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA)
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Bleeding assessment scores may be elevated

distinguishingFeatures: Normal neutrophil morphology without inclusion bodies
Absence of MYH9 mutations and inclusion bodies

redFlags: Severe bleeding episodes disproportionate to platelet count
Development of proteinuria or signs of renal failure
references: Pecci A, et al. MYH9-Related Disease: Clinical and Laboratory Features in 108 Patients. Haematologica. 2014.
Balduini CL, et al. MYH9-Related Disease: Diagnosis and Management. Haematologica. 2011.
Kunishima S, et al. MYH9 Disorders: Clinical Features and Molecular Pathogenesis. Int J Hematol. 2013.
